chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In the case of two men who had two dirhams with them, one of them said, 'The two dirhams are mine,' and the other said, 'They are between me and you.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for one of the two dirhams, he has no share in it, and indeed it belongs to its owner, and the second dirham is divided between them into two halves.'

key_terms.يُقْسَمُ: It is divided (legal division of assets)

ai.seo_question: How is property divided when two people claim ownership with conflicting assertions?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) applies the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) to resolve a dispute over two dirhams where one party claims sole ownership and the other claims joint ownership. The Imam decrees that the dirham with clear, undisputed ownership remains with the sole claimant, while the second dirham, subject to mutual claim, is divided equally. This precedent highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving financial ambiguities by prioritizing certainty (*yaqin*) over speculation, ensuring equitable distribution in cases of shared doubt.
